- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently fallen.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction to avoid excessive overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust downward quickly; apply a lagged correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods; if forecast is far above recent mean, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period when sentiment is high; apply a downward bias of 1–3% for first 7–10 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model often underperforms; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for lack of momentum.
